header.title: Suppl. Mag. 45: Erotic charm (applied love spell to bind Euphemia, daughter of Dorothea, for Theon, son of Proechia): AI translation (Claude)
header.author: Supplementum Magicum
header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's urn:magic:dclp:92236:grc, from papyri.info's Digital Corpus of Literary Papyri (CC BY 3.0), one English line for each line of the original. Only some passages are translated so far: those that the Atlas of Ancient Myth, Magic in the Ancient Texts and the demons-and-angels study cite.
header.statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.
header.availability: CC BY 4.0: credit papyri.info's Digital Corpus of Literary Papyri (the source's own licence is CC BY 3.0) and this AI translation.

notes.1: Magical names and vowel strings are kept as written; in Barbathiaō the last two letters are doubtful, and so are the last three letters of 'be able' in line 6. 'ἐγείρεσθαι' (4) is read as the imperative 'rise up'. 'ἐναρῶ' (18) is not a known verb; it is taken from its construction as a formula of adjuration, perhaps for ἐνορκῶ, 'I adjure'. 'The earth of the dogs' (16–17) is unclear: perhaps a place or a burial ground. The unit breaks off mid-word ('sanc-[tuaries]').

nodes.text: I bind you with the unbreakable bonds of Fate beneath the earth and of mighty Necessity, because I adjure
you, *daimones* [spirits of the dead], who lie here and are fed here and spend your time here,
and the youths here who died before their time. I adjure you by the uncon-
quered god Iaō Barbathiaō brimiaō chermari: rise up, daimones, you who here
lie, and seek out Euphemia, whom Dorothea bore, for Theon, whom Proechia bore;
the whole night through let her not be able to get sleep, but bring her, until she comes to the feet
of him, in love with a frenzied love, and with affection and intercourse. For I have bound her
brain and hands and abdomen and genitals and
heart to love of me, Theon. But if you disobey and do not quick-
ly accomplish what I tell you, the sun does not sink beneath the earth, and neither Hades
nor the world exists. But if you bring me Euphemia, whom Dorothea bore,
to me, Theon, whom Proechia bore, I will give you Osiris Nophriōth,
the brother of Isis, and he brings the cold water and will give rest to
your souls. But i[f] you do not accomplish for me what I tell you, there will burn you up
Eōnebyōth. I adjure you, daimones, who lie here: ieō
iiiiaia ēia iaō iaē iaō alilamps. I lay [this] down for you in the earth
of the dogs. Bind Euphemia to love of me, Theon,
